cards.title: A pixel that isn’t working
cards.label: flagged
evidence: Flagged NONFUNC (not working) and TRANSIENT by the pipeline
About 23,052 MJy/sr in one pixel, while the pixels around it read about 0.4
Nothing there in 18 of 18 other photos of the same sky within 5 days
cards.howToTell: A real source shows in the other photos of the same spot; a bad pixel shows in one.

cards.title: An afterglow on the detector
cards.label: flagged
evidence: Flagged PERSIST by the pipeline: light left on the detector by something bright it saw before
Nothing there in 16 of 16 other photos of the same sky within 5 days
cards.howToTell: If it isn’t in the other photos of the same spot and carries a persistence flag, it’s the detector remembering, not the sky.

cards.title: A star too bright for the detector
cards.looksLike: a strange blob or a spike
cards.label: confirmed
evidence: Barnard’s Star, Gaia DR3 G 8.2: far brighter than SPHEREx can measure
Flagged BLOOM and OVERFLOW at its centre (84 pixels) and HALO around it (130 pixels)
Its light is real; only the centre’s numbers can’t be trusted
cards.howToTell: A blob on a bright catalogued star with saturation flags is the star itself, not something new.

cards.title: An ordinary star (for comparison)
cards.label: confirmed
evidence: S/N 50; no artefact flags; no other Gaia star within 3 pixels
Also seen in another photo of the same spot (S/N 48)
cards.howToTell: A catalogued star that shows in every photo of the spot is just a star.

cards.title: Two sources in one pixel
cards.looksLike: one object, maybe a new one
cards.label: confirmed
evidence: WISE 0855 and a Gaia star (G 16.3) lie 6.4″ apart: about one SPHEREx pixel (6.15″)
At 1.1–1.6 µm the light is centred 0.7″ or less from the star
At 4.4–5 µm it moves to 3.5″ from the star and 2.9″ from WISE 0855’s predicted place
cards.howToTell: If a catalogued star sits within a pixel or two, the spot is a blend: look at its colours, as “Two colours” does on WISE 0855’s page.
